name: Curly Hair
description: Curly hair typically has a coiled or kinked texture, with more defined curls and less overall volume than other hair types. It can vary from loose waves to tightly coiled spirals.
porosity: Variable but generally high due to the shape of the cuticle scales, which can lead to issues like frizz and tangling.
characteristics: Higher porosity leading to potential dryness if not properly cared for
Naturally drier than straight hair due to the shape of the cuticle
washing_frequency: Every 2-3 days or as needed to avoid over-washing which can strip natural oils
oil_recommendation: Regular application of lightweight oils like jojoba or argan oil for added moisture and shine

morning_routine.action: Apply a leave-in conditioner or curl-defining cream to damp hair.
morning_routine.purpose: To enhance the definition and manageability of curls.

night_routine.action: Deep condition your hair once a week using a mask or intensive treatment.
night_routine.purpose: To hydrate and strengthen the hair overnight, promoting healthier growth.

weekly_care: Use a clarifying shampoo occasionally to remove product buildup and impurities.
heat_styling_recommendation: Limit heat styling to reduce damage. Use heat protectants when necessary.
foods_for_healthy_hair: Vitamins and minerals (e.g., biotin, zinc, iron)
common_mistakes: Using the wrong heat protection products
do: Regularly apply leave-in conditioners or scrunching creams
Use wide-tooth combs and fingers to detangle
Protect your curls during sleep with silk or satin pillowcases
dont: Rely too heavily on heat styling tools
Use products that are heavy or greasy
Ignore the need for moisture in curly hair

seasonal_care.summer: Stay hydrated, use lighter oils and avoid excessive sun exposure which can dry out curls.
seasonal_care.winter: Increase moisturizing routines to combat dry air and indoor heating.
seasonal_care.monsoon: Protect your curls from rain and humidity with hats or leave-in conditioners.

expert_tips: Experiment with different styling techniques to find what works best for your specific curl pattern.
Regularly visit a trichologist or dermatologist specializing in curly hair care for personalized advice.
